Extensible Markov Models for Sequence Data

Source: R/rEMM-package.R
rEMM-package.Rd

Model clusters and their temporal relationships using an extensible Markov chain. See vignette("rEMM") for a getting started guide.

Models

EMM combines data stream clustering with a temporal model. tNN provides threshold nearest neighbor clustering, and TRACDS learns temporal relationships from cluster assignments.

Temporal Structure for Standard Clustering Algorithms

TRAC adds a Markov model to an existing clustering of sequence data, such as a k-means or PAM clustering.

Building models

build adds observations to an EMM, cluster adds observations to a tNN clustering, and update adds cluster assignments to a temporal model.

Working with the models

plot visualizes a model, and find_clusters assigns observations to existing clusters without updating the model. recluster groups micro-clusters, and merge_clusters merges specified states.

remove removes specified states or transitions, prune removes rare states or transitions, and fade reduces the weight of older observations. combine combines EMMs.

Transitions and sequence analysis

transition accesses transition probabilities and counts, and transition_table extracts transitions for a new sequence. smooth_transitions smooths transition counts between neighboring states. score measures how well a sequence agrees with a model, and predict predicts future states.

Stream Interface

DSC_EMM and DSC_tNN provide clusterers for the stream framework.

Data

synthetic_stream generates synthetic sequence data. Bundled examples include EMMsim (simulated sequences), EMMTraffic (hypothetical traffic observations), Derwent (river flow readings), and rRNA16S (16S rRNA sequence counts).
